verses.text: Di words of Jeremiah, Hilkiah pikin, one of di priests wey dey Anathoth for di land of Benjamin,
to whom di word of di Lord come for di days of Josiah, Amon pikin, king of Judah, for di thirteenth year of im reign.
E come also for di days of Jehoiakim, Josiah pikin, king of Judah, to di end of di eleventh year of Zedekiah, Josiah pikin, king of Judah, to di carrying away of Jerusalem captive for di fifth month.
Now di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Before I form you for di belly, I know you. Before you come out of di womb, I sanctify you. I don appoint you prophet to di nations.”
Den I talk, “Ah, Lord God! See, I no know how to speak, because I be child.”
But di Lord talk to me, “No talk say, ‘I be child,’ because to everyone wey I send you to, you go go, and wetin I command you, you go speak.
No dey afraid because of dem, because I dey with you to deliver you,” talk di Lord.
Den di Lord put out im hand, and touch my mouth. Di Lord talk to me, “See, I don put my words for your mouth.
See, I don set you dis day over di nations and over di kingdoms, to uproot and to break down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant.”
Moreover di word of di Lord come to me, say, “Jeremiah, wetin you see?” I talk, “I see rod of almond tree.”
Den di Lord talk to me, “You don see well, because I dey watch over my word to perform am.”
Di word of di Lord come to me di second time, say, “Wetin you see?” I talk, “I see boiling pot, and im face dey from di north.”
Den di Lord talk to me, “Out of di north disaster go break out on all di inhabitants of di land.

Because see, I go call all di families of di kingdoms of di north,” talk di Lord. “Dem go come, and dem go set everyone im throne at di entrance of di gates of Jerusalem, and against all im walls all round, and against all di cities of Judah.
I go pronounce my judgments against dem touching all dem wickedness, in that dem don forsake me, and don burn incense to other gods, and worship di works of dem own hands.
Therefore gird up your loins, and arise, and speak to dem all wey I command you. No dey dismayed at dem, lest I dismay you before dem.

Because see, I don make you dis day like fortified city, like iron pillar, and like bronze walls against di whole land, against di kings of Judah, against im princes, against im priests, and against di people of di land.
Dem go fight against you, but dem no go prevail against you, because I dey with you,” talk di Lord, “to deliver you.”
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,

“Go, and cry for di ears of Jerusalem, say, ‘Di Lord talk like dis: I remember for you di kindness of your youth, di love of your betrothal, how you follow me for di wilderness, for land wey dem no sow.
Israel na holiness to di Lord, di first fruits of im harvest. All wey devour am go dey held guilty. Disaster go come on dem,’” talk di Lord.
Hear di word of di Lord, house of Jacob, and all di families of di house of Israel.
Di Lord talk like dis: “Wetin wrong dey inside me wey una fathers don find, say dem don go far from me, and don follow after worthless things, and become worthless?

Dem no talk, ‘Where di Lord dey wey bring us up out of di land of Egypt, wey lead us through di wilderness, through land of deserts and of pits, through land of drought and of di shadow of death, through land wey nobody pass, and where no man dwell?’
I bring una into plentiful land, to eat im fruit and im goodness. But when una enter, una defile my land, and make my heritage abomination.
Di priests no talk, ‘Where di Lord dey?’ Dem wey handle di law no know me. Di rulers also transgress against me. Di prophets prophesy by Baal, and waka after things wey no profit.
Therefore I go still contend with una,” talk di Lord, “and I go contend with una children children.
Because cross over to di coasts of Kittim, and see. Send to Kedar, and consider diligently. See whether any such thing as dis don dey.
Nation don change im gods, wey no be gods? But my people don change dem glory for wetin no profit.
Be astonished, una heavens, at dis, and dey horribly afraid. Dey very desolate,” talk di Lord.
“Because my people don commit two evils: dem don forsake me, di spring of living waters, and dug cisterns for demselves, broken cisterns, wey no fit hold water.
Israel na servant? Na slave wey dem born for house? Why e don become prey?
Di young lions don roar at am, and yelled. Dem don make im land waste. Im cities dey burned up, without inhabitant.
Di people of Memphis and Tahpanhes don also break di crown of your head.
Una no don bring dis on yourselves, in that una don forsake di Lord your God, when e lead you by di way?
Now why you go di way to Egypt, to drink di waters of di Shihor? Or why you go di way to Assyria, to drink di waters of di River?

Your own wickedness go correct you, and your backsliding go rebuke you. Know therefore and see say na evil and bitter thing say you don forsake di Lord your God, and say my fear no dey for you,” talk di Lord, di Lord of Armies.
“Because of old time I don break your yoke, and burst your bonds. You talk, ‘I no go serve.’ Because on every high hill and under every green tree you don bow, as prostitute.
Yet I plant you as noble vine, wholly right seed. How den you don turn to me into degenerate shoots of foreign vine?
Because though you wash yourself with lye, and use much soap, yet your iniquity dey marked before me,” talk di Lord God.
“How you fit talk, ‘I no dey polluted, I no go after di Baals’? See your way for di valley. Know wetin you don do, you swift young camel wey dey run here and dere,
wild donkey used to di wilderness, wey sniff di wind for im desire. For im time of mating, who fit turn am away? All dem wey seek am no go weary demselves. For im month dem go find am.
Keep your foot from being unshod, and your throat from thirst. But you talk, ‘E dey hopeless. No, because I don love strangers, and after dem I go go.’
As di thief dey ashamed when e dey caught, so di house of Israel dey ashamed: dem, dem kings, dem princes, and dem priests, and dem prophets,
wey talk to wood, ‘You na my papa,’ and to stone, ‘You don bring me forth.’ Because dem don turn dem back to me, and no dem face. But for di time of dem trouble dem go talk, ‘Arise, and save us.’
But where dem gods wey you don make for yourself dey? Make dem arise, if dem fit save you for di time of your trouble. Because according to di number of your cities na your gods, Judah.
Why una go plead with me? Una all don rebel against me,” talk di Lord.
“I don strike una children in vain. Dem no receive correction. Your own sword don devour your prophets, like destroying lion.
Generation, see di word of di Lord. I don be wilderness to Israel? Or land of thick darkness? Why my people talk, ‘We dey free. We go no more come to you’?
Di virgin fit forget her ornaments, or di bride her attire? Yet my people don forget me days without number.
How well you fit direct your way to seek love! Therefore even di wicked women you don teach your ways.
Also on your skirts dey found di blood of di souls of di innocent poor. You no catch dem breaking in. But despite all dis,
yet you talk, ‘I dey innocent. Surely im anger don turn away from me.’ See, I go enter judgment with you, because you talk, ‘I no don sin.’
Why you dey go about so much to change your way? You go dey ashamed of Egypt also, as you dey ashamed of Assyria.
From dere also you go go out with your hands on your head, because di Lord don reject di things wey you trust, and you no go prosper for dem.”

“If man divorce im wife, and she leave am, and become another man own, e go return to her again? No be say dat land go dey greatly polluted? But you don play di prostitute with many lovers. Yet return to me,” talk di Lord.

“Lift up your eyes to di bare heights, and see. Where dem no lie with you? For di roads you don sit for dem like Arabian for di wilderness. You don pollute di land with your prostitution and with your wickedness.
Therefore di showers don dey withheld, and no latter rain dey. Yet you get prostitute forehead. You refuse to dey ashamed.
You no just now cry to me, ‘My Papa, you na di guide of my youth.
E go dey angry forever? E go keep am to di end?’ See, you don speak and don do evil things, and don have your way.”

Moreover di Lord talk to me for di days of Josiah di king, “You don see wetin backsliding Israel don do? She don go up on every high mountain and under every green tree, and don play di prostitute dere.
I talk, after she don do all dis, ‘She go return to me.’ But she no return. Her treacherous sister Judah see am.

I see say, for all di causes whereby backsliding Israel don commit adultery, I don put her away and give her certificate of divorce. Yet her treacherous sister Judah no fear, but she go also play di prostitute.
Because of di lightness of her prostitution, di land dey polluted, and she don commit adultery with stones and with wood.
Yet for all dis her treacherous sister Judah no return to me with her whole heart, but in pretense,” talk di Lord.
Di Lord talk to me, “Backsliding Israel don show imself more righteous pass treacherous Judah.

Go, and proclaim dis words toward di north, and talk, ‘Return, backsliding Israel,’ talk di Lord. ‘I no go cause my face to fall on una, because I dey merciful,’ talk di Lord. ‘I no go keep anger forever.
Only acknowledge your iniquity, say you don transgress against di Lord your God, and don scatter your ways to di strangers under every green tree, and una no obey my voice,’ talk di Lord.
Return, backsliding children,” talk di Lord, “because I be husband to una. I go take una, one of one city, and two of one family, and I go bring una to Zion.
I go give una shepherds according to my heart, wey go feed una with knowledge and understanding.

E go happen, when una multiply and increase for di land, for dose days,” talk di Lord, “dem no go talk again, ‘Di ark of di covenant of di Lord.’ E no go come to mind. Dem no go remember am. Dem no go miss am, neither dem go make another.
For dat time dem go call Jerusalem di throne of di Lord. All di nations go dey gathered to am, to di name of di Lord, to Jerusalem. Dem no go waka again after di stubbornness of dem evil heart.
For dose days di house of Judah go waka with di house of Israel, and dem go come together out of di land of di north to di land wey I give for inheritance to una fathers.”
“But I talk, ‘How I go put you among di children, and give you pleasant land, di most beautiful heritage of di nations?’ I talk, ‘You go call me “My Papa,” and no go turn away from following me.’”
“Surely as wife treacherously leave her husband, so una don deal treacherously with me, house of Israel,” talk di Lord.
Voice dey heard on di bare heights, di weeping and di supplications of di children of Israel, because dem don pervert dem way. Dem don forget di Lord dem God.
“Return, una backsliding children, I go heal una backsliding.” “See, we come to you, because you be di Lord our God.
Truly di hills dey vain, di confusion of di mountains. Truly for di Lord our God na di salvation of Israel.
But di shameful thing don devour di labour of our fathers from our youth: dem flocks and dem herds, dem sons and dem daughters.

Make we lie down for our shame, and make our dishonour cover us, because we don sin against di Lord our God, we and our fathers, from our youth even to dis day, and we no obey di voice of di Lord our God.”
“If you go return, Israel,” talk di Lord, “return to me. If you go put away your abominations from my sight, den you no go wander.
You go swear, ‘As di Lord live,’ in truth, in justice, and in righteousness. Den di nations go bless demselves in am, and in am dem go glory.”
Because di Lord talk like dis to di men of Judah and to Jerusalem: “Break up your fallow ground, and no sow among thorns.

Circumcise yourselves to di Lord, and take away di foreskins of your heart, una men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, lest my wrath go out like fire, and burn so that none fit quench am, because of di evil of una doings.
Declare for Judah, and publish for Jerusalem, and talk, ‘Blow di trumpet for di land!’ Cry aloud and talk, ‘Gather yourselves together, and make we go into di fortified cities.’
Set up di standard toward Zion. Flee for safety. No stay, because I go bring evil from di north, and great destruction.
Lion don go up from im thicket, and di destroyer of nations don set out. E don go out from im place to make your land desolate, so that your cities go dey laid waste, without inhabitant.
For dis gird una yourselves with sackcloth, lament and howl, because di fierce anger of di Lord never turn back from us.
E go happen for dat day,” talk di Lord, “say di heart of di king go perish, and di heart of di princes. Di priests go dey astonished, and di prophets go wonder.”
Den I talk, “Ah, Lord God! Surely you don greatly deceive dis people and Jerusalem, saying, ‘Una go get peace,’ whereas di sword reach to di heart.”
For dat time dem go talk to dis people and to Jerusalem, “Hot wind from di bare heights for di wilderness toward di daughter of my people, no to winnow, nor to cleanse.
Full wind from dose places go come for me. Now I go also pronounce judgments against dem.”
See, e go come up like clouds, and im chariots like di whirlwind. Im horses dey swifter pass eagles. Woe to us, because we dey ruined!
Jerusalem, wash your heart from wickedness, so that you go dey saved. How long your evil thoughts go lodge inside you?
Because voice declare from Dan, and publish evil from di hills of Ephraim.
“Tell di nations. See, publish against Jerusalem, say besiegers dey come from far country, and dem raise dem voice against di cities of Judah.
As keepers of field, dem dey against her round about, because she don rebel against me,” talk di Lord.
“Your way and your doings don bring dis things on you. Dis na your wickedness. Surely e dey bitter, surely e reach to your heart.”
My anguish, my anguish! I dey in pain for my heart. My heart dey pound for me. I no fit hold my peace, because you don hear, my soul, di sound of di trumpet, di alarm of war.
Destruction on destruction dey proclaimed, because di whole land dey laid waste. Suddenly my tents dey destroyed, and my curtains for moment.
How long I go see di standard, and hear di sound of di trumpet?
“Because my people dey foolish. Dem no know me. Dem na foolish children, and dem no get understanding. Dem dey wise to do evil, but to do good dem no know how.”
I look on di earth, and see, e dey waste and void. I look to di heavens, and dem no get light.
I look on di mountains, and see, dem dey tremble, and all di hills dey move back and forth.
I look, and see, no man dey, and all di birds of di sky don flee.
I look, and see, di fruitful land na wilderness, and all im cities dey broken down at di presence of di Lord, and at im fierce anger.
Because di Lord talk like dis: “Di whole land go dey desolate, yet I no go make full end.
For dis di earth go mourn, and di heavens above go dey black, because I don speak am. I don purpose am, and I no go relent, neither go turn back from am.”
Every city dey flee for di noise of di horsemen and bowmen. Dem go into di thickets, and climb up among di rocks. Every city dey forsaken, and no man dwell inside dem.

You wey don dey desolate, wetin you go do? Though you dress yourself in scarlet, though you decorate yourself with ornaments of gold, though you enlarge your eyes with paint, for vain you make yourself beautiful. Your lovers despise you. Dem seek your life.

Because I don hear voice as of woman for labour, di anguish as of her wey dey bring forth her first child, di voice of di daughter of Zion wey gasp for breath, wey spread her hands, “Woe to me now! Because my soul faint before murderers.”
“Run to and fro through di streets of Jerusalem. See now, and know, and seek for im squares, if una fit find man, if any dey wey do justly, wey seek truth, and I go pardon am.
Though dem talk, ‘As di Lord live,’ surely dem swear falsely.”

Di Lord, no your eyes dey on truth? You don strike dem, but dem no grieve. You don consume dem, but dem refuse to receive correction. Dem don make dem faces harder pass rock. Dem don refuse to return.
Den I talk, “Surely dis na poor people. Dem dey foolish, because dem no know di way of di Lord, nor di law of dem God.
I go get me to di great men, and go speak to dem, because dem know di way of di Lord, and di law of dem God.” But dem all don together break di yoke, and burst di bonds.

Therefore lion out of di forest go kill dem, wolf of di evenings go destroy dem, leopard go watch against dem cities. Everyone wey go out from dere go dey torn in pieces, because dem transgressions many, and dem backslidings don increase.

“How I go pardon you for dis? Your children don forsake me, and sworn by dem wey no be gods. When I don feed dem to di full, dem commit adultery, and assemble demselves by troops for di prostitute houses.
Dem be like fed horses wey dey roam. Everyone dey neigh after im neighbour wife.
I no go visit for dis things?” talk di Lord. “My soul no go dey avenged on such nation as dis?
Go up on her walls, and destroy, but no make full end. Take away her branches, because dem no be di Lord own.
Because di house of Israel and di house of Judah don deal very treacherously against me,” talk di Lord.
Dem don deny di Lord, and talk, “E no be am. Evil no go come on us. We no go see sword or famine.
Di prophets go become wind, and di word no dey for dem. Make am dey done to dem.”
Therefore di Lord, di God of Armies, talk like dis: “Because una don speak dis word, see, I go make my words for your mouth fire, and dis people wood, and e go devour dem.
See, I go bring nation on una from far, house of Israel,” talk di Lord. “E na mighty nation. E na ancient nation, nation wey una no know im language, neither understand wetin dem talk.
Dem quiver na open grave. Dem all na mighty men.

Dem go eat up your harvest and your bread, wey your sons and your daughters suppose eat. Dem go eat up your flocks and your herds. Dem go eat up your vines and your fig trees. Dem go beat down your fortified cities, wey you trust, with di sword.
But even for dose days,” talk di Lord, “I no go make full end of una.

E go happen, when una talk, ‘Why di Lord our God don do all dis to us?’ den you go talk to dem, ‘Like how una don forsake me, and serve foreign gods for una land, so una go serve strangers for land wey no be una own.’
Declare dis for di house of Jacob, and publish am for Judah, say,
‘Hear dis now, foolish people, without understanding, wey get eyes, but no see, wey get ears, but no hear:

Una no fear me?’ talk di Lord. ‘Una no go tremble at my presence, wey don place di sand as di bound of di sea, by perpetual decree, so that e no fit pass? Though di waves toss, yet dem no fit prevail. Though dem roar, yet dem no fit pass over am.
But dis people get revolting and rebellious heart. Dem don revolt and gone.
Dem no talk for dem heart, “Make we now fear di Lord our God, wey give rain, both di former and di latter, for im season, wey keep for us di appointed weeks of di harvest.”
Una iniquities don turn away dis things, and una sins don withhold good from una.
Because among my people dey found wicked men. Dem lie in wait, as one wey set snares. Dem set trap. Dem catch men.
As cage full of birds, so dem houses full of deceit. Therefore dem don become great, and grow rich.
Dem don grow fat. Dem shine. Yes, dem overpass di deeds of di wicked. Dem no plead di cause, di cause of di fatherless, so that dem go prosper, and di right of di needy dem no judge.
I no go visit for dis things?’ talk di Lord. ‘My soul no go dey avenged on such nation as dis?’
Astonishing and horrible thing don happen for di land:
di prophets prophesy falsely, and di priests rule by dem own authority, and my people love to have am so. And wetin una go do for di end of am?”

“Flee for safety, una children of Benjamin, out of di middle of Jerusalem, and blow di trumpet for Tekoa, and set up sign of fire for Beth Haccherem, because evil dey look out from di north, and great destruction.
I don cut off di daughter of Zion, di lovely and delicate one.
Shepherds with dem flocks go come to her. Dem go pitch dem tents against her all round. Dem go feed everyone for im place.
Prepare war against her. Arise, make we go up at noon! Woe to us, because di day decline, because di shadows of evening dey stretch out.
Arise, make we go up by night, and make we destroy her palaces.”
Because di Lord of Armies talk like dis: “Cut down trees, and cast mound against Jerusalem. Dis na di city wey must dey visited. Inside am dey only oppression.
As spring dey cast out im waters, so e cast out her wickedness. Violence and destruction dey heard inside her. Before me continually dey grief and wounds.
Be instructed, Jerusalem, lest my soul dey alienated from you, lest I make you desolate, land wey no dey inhabited.”
Di Lord of Armies talk like dis: “Dem go thoroughly glean di remnant of Israel like vine. Turn back your hand like grape gatherer into di baskets.”
To who I go speak and give warning, so that dem go hear? See, dem ear dey uncircumcised, and dem no fit listen. See, di word of di Lord don become to dem reproach. Dem no delight for am.

But I dey full of di wrath of di Lord. I dey weary with holding in. “Pour am out on di children for di street, and on di assembly of young men together, because even di husband with di wife go dey taken, di aged with am wey dey full of days.
Dem houses go dey turned to others, dem fields and dem wives together, because I go stretch out my hand against di inhabitants of di land,” talk di Lord.
“Because from di least of dem even to di greatest of dem, everyone dey given to covetousness. From di prophet even to di priest, everyone deal falsely.
Dem don heal di wound of my people slightly, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when peace no dey.

Dem dey ashamed say dem don commit abomination? No, dem no dey ashamed at all. Dem no even know how to blush. Therefore dem go fall among dem wey fall. For di time wey I visit dem, dem go dey cast down,” talk di Lord.
Di Lord talk like dis: “Stand for di ways and see, and ask for di ancient paths, where di good way dey, and waka for am, and una go find rest for una souls. But dem talk, ‘We no go waka for am.’
I set watchmen over una, saying, ‘Listen to di sound of di trumpet!’ But dem talk, ‘We no go listen.’
Therefore hear, una nations, and know, congregation, wetin dey among dem.
Hear, earth! See, I go bring evil on dis people, even di fruit of dem thoughts, because dem no listen to my words, and as for my law, dem reject am.
Wetin incense from Sheba and sweet cane from far country mean to me? Una burnt offerings no dey acceptable, neither una sacrifices sweet to me.”
Therefore di Lord talk like dis: “See, I go lay stumbling blocks before dis people. Di fathers and di sons together go stumble on dem. Neighbour and friend go perish.”
Di Lord talk like dis: “See, people dey come from di north country, and great nation go dey stirred up from di uttermost parts of di earth.
Dem lay hold on bow and spear. Dem dey cruel, and no mercy dey for dem. Dem voice roar like di sea, and dem ride on horses, set in array, as man for battle, against you, daughter of Zion.”
We don hear di report of am. Our hands hang limp. Anguish don seize us, and pain as of woman for labour.
No go out into di field, nor waka on di way, because di sword of di enemy and terror dey on every side.
Daughter of my people, gird on sackcloth, and wallow for ashes. Mourn as for only son, with bitter lamentation, because di destroyer go suddenly come on us.
“I don set you as assayer and refiner among my people, so that you go know and try dem way.
Dem all na grievous rebels, going about with slander. Dem na bronze and iron. Dem all dey corrupt.
Di bellows blow fiercely. Di lead dey consumed by di fire. For nothing e dey refine, because di wicked no dey plucked away.
Dem go call dem rejected silver, because di Lord don reject dem.”
Di word wey come to Jeremiah from di Lord, say,
“Stand for di gate of di Lord house, and proclaim dere dis word, and talk, ‘Hear di word of di Lord, all una of Judah, wey enter dis gates to worship di Lord.’”
Di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: “Amend una ways and una doings, and I go cause una to dwell for dis place.
No trust for lying words, saying, ‘Di temple of di Lord, di temple of di Lord, di temple of di Lord, na dis.’
Because if una thoroughly amend una ways and una doings, if una thoroughly execute justice between man and im neighbour,
if una no oppress di foreigner, di fatherless, and di widow, and no shed innocent blood for dis place, neither waka after other gods to una own hurt,
den I go cause una to dwell for dis place, for di land wey I gave to una fathers, from of old even forever.
See, una trust for lying words wey no profit.
Una go steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, burn incense to Baal, and waka after other gods wey una no know,
and come and stand before me for dis house, wey dem call by my name, and talk, ‘We dey safe,’ so that una go do all dis abominations?
Dis house, wey dem call by my name, don become den of robbers for una eyes? See, I, even I, don see am,” talk di Lord.
“But go now to my place wey dey Shiloh, where I make my name dwell at di first, and see wetin I do to am because of di wickedness of my people Israel.
Now, because una don do all dis works,” talk di Lord, “and I speak to una, rising up early and speaking, but una no hear, and I call una, but una no answer,
therefore I go do to di house wey dem call by my name, wey una trust, and to di place wey I give to una and to una fathers, as I do to Shiloh.
I go cast una out of my sight, as I don cast out all una brothers, even di whole offspring of Ephraim.”
“Therefore no pray for dis people, neither lift up cry nor prayer for dem, neither make intercession to me, because I no go hear you.
Una no see wetin dem dey do for di cities of Judah and for di streets of Jerusalem?
Di children gather wood, di fathers kindle di fire, and di women knead dough, to make cakes to di queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings to other gods, so that dem go provoke me to anger.
Na me dem dey provoke?” talk di Lord. “No be demselves, to di shame of dem own faces?”

Therefore di Lord God talk like dis: “See, my anger and my wrath go dey poured out on dis place, on man and on animal, and on di trees of di field, and on di fruit of di ground. E go burn, and no go dey quenched.”
Di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: “Add una burnt offerings to una sacrifices, and eat flesh.
Because I no speak to una fathers, nor command dem, for di day wey I bring dem out of di land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices.
But dis na wetin I command dem, saying, ‘Obey my voice, and I go be una God, and una go be my people. Waka for all di way wey I command una, so that e go dey well with una.’
But dem no listen, nor incline dem ear, but waka for dem own counsels and for di stubbornness of dem evil heart, and go backward, and no forward.
From di day wey una fathers come out of di land of Egypt to dis day, I don send to una all my servants di prophets, daily rising up early and sending dem.
Yet dem no listen to me, nor incline dem ear, but stiffen dem neck. Dem do worse pass dem fathers.
Therefore you go speak all dis words to dem, but dem no go listen to you. You go also call to dem, but dem no go answer you.
You go talk to dem, ‘Dis na di nation wey no obey di voice of di Lord dem God, nor receive instruction. Truth don perish, and e don dey cut off from dem mouth.
Cut off your hair, and throw am away, and take up lamentation for di bare heights, because di Lord don reject and forsake di generation of im wrath.’
Because di children of Judah don do evil for my sight,” talk di Lord. “Dem don set dem abominations for di house wey dem call by my name, to defile am.
Dem don build di high places of Topheth, wey dey di valley of di son of Hinnom, to burn dem sons and dem daughters for fire, wey I no command, neither e come into my mind.
Therefore see, di days dey come,” talk di Lord, “wey e no go dey called Topheth, nor di valley of di son of Hinnom, but di valley of Slaughter, because dem go bury for Topheth, till no room dey.
Di dead bodies of dis people go be food for di birds of di sky, and for di animals of di earth. None go frighten dem away.

Den I go cause to cease from di cities of Judah and from di streets of Jerusalem di voice of mirth and di voice of gladness, di voice of di bridegroom and di voice of di bride, because di land go dey desolate.”

“For dat time,” talk di Lord, “dem go bring out di bones of di kings of Judah, di bones of im princes, di bones of di priests, di bones of di prophets, and di bones of di inhabitants of Jerusalem, out of dem graves.

Dem go spread dem before di sun, di moon, and all di army of heaven, wey dem don love, and wey dem don serve, and after wey dem don waka, and wey dem don seek, and wey dem don worship. Dem no go dey gathered, nor buried. Dem go be like dung on di surface of di ground.
Death go dey chosen rather pass life by all di remnant wey remain of dis evil family, for all di places wey I don drive dem to,” talk di Lord of Armies.
“Moreover you go talk to dem, ‘Di Lord talk like dis: Dem wey fall no go rise again? Dem wey turn away no go return?
Why den dis people of Jerusalem don turn away with perpetual backsliding? Dem hold fast to deceit. Dem refuse to return.
I listen and hear, but dem no speak right. No man repent of im wickedness, saying, “Wetin I don do?” Everyone turn to im course, as horse wey rush into battle.
Yes, di stork for di sky know im appointed times. Di turtledove, di swallow and di crane observe di time of dem coming, but my people no know di law of di Lord.
How una fit talk, “We dey wise, and di law of di Lord dey with us”? But see, di false pen of di scribes don turn am into lie.
Di wise men dey ashamed. Dem dey dismayed and caught. See, dem don reject di word of di Lord, and wetin wisdom dem get?

Therefore I go give dem wives to other men, and dem fields to dem wey go possess dem, because everyone from di least even to di greatest dey given to covetousness. From di prophet even to di priest, everyone deal falsely.
Dem don heal di hurt of di daughter of my people slightly, saying, “Peace, peace,” when peace no dey.

Dem dey ashamed say dem don commit abomination? No, dem no dey ashamed at all, neither dem know how to blush. Therefore dem go fall among dem wey fall. For di time of dem visitation dem go dey cast down,’” talk di Lord.
“I go surely consume dem,” talk di Lord. “No grapes dey on di vine, nor figs on di fig tree, and di leaf don fade. Wetin I don give dem don pass away from dem.”

“Why we dey sit still? Gather yourselves together, and make we enter di fortified cities, and dey silent dere, because di Lord our God don put us to silence, and give us poisoned water to drink, because we don sin against di Lord.
We look for peace, but no good come, and for time of healing, and see, terror!

Di snorting of im horses dey heard from Dan. All di land tremble at di sound of di neighing of im strong ones, because dem don come, and don devour di land and all wey dey inside am, di city and dem wey dwell inside am.”
“Because see, I go send serpents among una, adders wey no go dey charmed, and dem go bite una,” talk di Lord.
Oh, my comfort against sorrow! My heart dey faint inside me.

See, di voice of di cry of di daughter of my people from di land wey dey far off: “Di Lord no dey for Zion? Im King no dey inside am?” “Why dem don provoke me to anger with dem engraved images, and with foreign vanities?”
“Di harvest don pass. Di summer don end, and we never dey saved.”
For di hurt of di daughter of my people I dey hurt. I dey mourning. Dismay don seize me.
Balm no dey for Gilead? Physician no dey dere? Why den di health of di daughter of my people no dey restored?
Oh say my head na water, and my eyes fountain of tears, so that I go weep day and night for di slain of di daughter of my people!
Oh say I get lodging place for travelers for di wilderness, so that I go leave my people, and go from dem! Because dem all na adulterers, assembly of treacherous men.
“Dem bend dem tongue like dem bow. Lies, and no truth, dey rule for di land. Because dem proceed from evil to evil, and dem no know me,” talk di Lord.
“Everyone take heed to im neighbour, and no trust any brother, because every brother go surely deceive, and every neighbour go walk with slander.
Everyone go deceive im neighbour, and no go speak truth. Dem don teach dem tongue to speak lies. Dem weary demselves to commit iniquity.
Your dwelling dey for di midst of deceit. Through deceit dem refuse to know me,” talk di Lord.
Therefore di Lord of Armies talk like dis: “See, I go refine dem, and try dem, because how else I go do, because of di daughter of my people?
Dem tongue na deadly arrow. E speak deceit. One speak peaceably to im neighbour with im mouth, but for im heart e lay in wait for am.
I no go visit dem for dis things?” talk di Lord. “I no go avenge myself on such nation as dis?”

I go take up weeping and wailing for di mountains, and lamentation for di pastures of di wilderness, because dem don burn up, so that no one pass through. Neither dem hear di voice of di cattle. Both di birds of di sky and di animals don flee, dem don go.
“I go make Jerusalem heaps, den of jackals, and I go make di cities of Judah desolate, without inhabitant.”

Who be di wise man wey fit understand dis? And who be im to whom di mouth of di Lord don speak, so that e fit declare am? Why di land perish and dey burned up like wilderness, so that no one pass through?
Di Lord talk, “Because dem don forsake my law wey I set before dem, and no obey my voice, neither waka inside am,
but don waka after di stubbornness of dem own heart, and after di Baals, wey dem fathers teach dem,”
therefore di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: “See, I go feed dem, even dis people, with wormwood, and give dem poisoned water to drink.
I go scatter dem also among di nations, wey neither dem nor dem fathers don know. I go send di sword after dem, until I don consume dem.”
Di Lord of Armies talk like dis: “Consider, and call for di mourning women, so that dem go come. Send for di skilful women, so that dem go come.
Make dem hurry, and take up wailing for us, so that our eyes go run down with tears, and our eyelids gush out with waters.
Because voice of wailing dey heard from Zion, ‘How we dey ruined! We dey greatly confounded, because we don forsake di land, because dem don cast down our dwellings.’”
Yet hear di word of di Lord, una women, and make una ear receive di word of im mouth. Teach una daughters wailing, and everyone her neighbour lamentation.
Because death don come up into our windows. E don enter our palaces, to cut off di children from di streets, and di young men from di squares.
Talk, “Di Lord talk like dis: ‘Di dead bodies of men go fall as dung on di open field, and as sheaf after di harvester, and nobody go gather dem.’”
Di Lord talk like dis: “No make di wise man glory for im wisdom, neither make di mighty man glory for im might. No make di rich man glory for im riches.

But make di one wey glory glory for dis: say e understand and know me, say I be di Lord wey exercise lovingkindness, justice and righteousness for di earth, because for dis things I delight,” talk di Lord.
“See, di days dey come,” talk di Lord, “wey I go punish all dem wey dey circumcised in uncircumcision:

Egypt, Judah, Edom, di children of Ammon, Moab, and all dem wey dey di farthest corners, wey dwell for di wilderness. Because all di nations dey uncircumcised, and all di house of Israel dey uncircumcised for heart.”
